issue: PWSID column in Q1 Base and Q1 LSLR files is numeric (e.g., 5282002, 5202020), so after fread with colClasses='character' it will be a plain 7-digit string. The script splits on '[,\n]' then prepends 'IN', producing e.g. 'IN5282002' (8 digits). However the Q4 Comprehensive and Q4 LSLR files have PWSID as a character string already formatted without leading zeros issues but still plain digits. The Tipton fix corrects 'IN528004' -> 'IN5280004', implying a leading-zero is being dropped somewhere for that entry. Numeric fread of '5280004' would store as 5280004 (7 digits) and produce 'IN5280004' correctly — but if the raw CSV has '05280004' or similar, numeric parsing would strip the leading zero to 5280004, producing 'IN5280004' which is fine. Need to verify whether any PWSID values in any file have leading zeros that numeric coercion would drop before 'IN' is prepended.
suggestion: Read PWSID columns explicitly as character in all files to prevent any leading-zero loss. Since colClasses='character' is already set globally via fread, confirm the numeric PWSID column in Q1 files does not have entries that depend on leading zeros; cross-check the Tipton PWSID raw value in the CSV.

issue: Q4 Comprehensive and Q4 LSLR files have PWSID as character (e.g., '5235001') with no commas or newlines visible in samples, but the column name in the Q4 files is 'PWSID\nNo' (with a newline) while Q1 files have 'PWSID\nNo' as well. After janitor::clean_names() both become 'pwsid_no'. However, in Q4 LSLR the PWSID column is numeric per the column summary (range=[5202020, 5271009]), so a multi-PWSID value separated by comma or newline would fail numeric parsing entirely and be read as NA. If any project has multiple PWSIDs, they would be silently lost.
suggestion: Confirm no multi-PWSID entries exist in Q4 LSLR. If they do, force that column to character before splitting.

issue: In Q4 Comprehensive, the 'Emerging Contaminants?' column contains values like 'Yes - PFAS', 'Yes - Mn', 'Yes', and 'TBD' — not simply 'Yes' or 'No'. The script checks grepl('Yes', emerging_contaminants, ignore.case=TRUE) which correctly matches 'Yes - PFAS' and 'Yes - Mn'. However, 'TBD' is not matched, so projects with 'TBD' in this field are silently treated as non-EC unless the project_description triggers the ec_str regex. This may misclassify some projects.
suggestion: Document that 'TBD' in Emerging Contaminants? is treated as non-EC unless description matches. If TBD should be treated differently (e.g., 'No Information'), add an explicit case_when branch for it.

issue: In Q4 Comprehensive and Q4 LSLR files, 'Lead Service Line Replacement Cost' is a character column with dollar-formatted values like '$1,669,000', '$0'. The script calls convert_to_numeric(lead_service_line_replacement_cost, TRUE) > 0 for project_type classification. If convert_to_numeric does not strip '$' and ',' before coercion, the result will be NA, and the > 0 comparison will return FALSE (NA > 0 is NA, treated as FALSE in case_when), potentially misclassifying lead projects as General.
suggestion: Ensure convert_to_numeric() strips currency symbols and commas before numeric conversion. Verify with a value like '$1,669,000' that the function returns 1669000.

issue: The script uses case_when: if is.na(requested_funds) use estimated_total_project_cost, else use requested_funds. In Q4 Comprehensive, 'Requested Funds' has 6.8% NA (the 'APPLICATIONS ONLY' rows) and 'Estimated Total Project Cost' has 93.2% NA. Both columns are character with dollar-formatted strings like '$28,454,000'. The clean_numeric_string() function must handle '$' and ',' stripping. If it doesn't, all requested_amount values from Q4 Comprehensive will be NA or wrong.
suggestion: Confirm clean_numeric_string() removes '$' and ',' characters. Test with '$200,000,000' and '$28,454,000'.

issue: PPL Rank in Q4 Comprehensive is a character column (not numeric) with 6.8% NA. The script checks is.na(ppl_rank) | ppl_rank == '-' to assign 'No Information'. The 6.8% NA rows correspond to the 'APPLICATIONS ONLY' section per the data dictionary, which should get 'No Information'. This appears handled. However, if any rank values contain unexpected strings (e.g., whitespace-only), they would pass through as-is rather than being normalized.
suggestion: Add a check for blank/whitespace-only ppl_rank values alongside the '-' check, e.g., trimws(ppl_rank) == '' or ppl_rank == '-'.

issue: Project descriptions in Q1 Base contain embedded newlines (e.g., 'Storage, Distribution, and Supply Improvements + Lead\nService Line Replacement'). The script applies str_squish() which collapses internal whitespace including newlines into single spaces. This should work correctly, but the 'lead' detection regex (grepl('lsl|lead', project_description, ignore.case=TRUE)) is applied after str_squish, so the newline in 'Lead\nService Line Replacement' becomes a space first — no issue with matching 'lead' but worth confirming str_squish runs before grepl in the mutate chain.
suggestion: Confirm project_description str_squish is applied in the same mutate block before project_type classification, or that project_type case_when references the already-squished column.

issue: The ec_str pattern reportedly includes 'Mn' (manganese). The Q4 Comprehensive data shows 'Yes - Mn' in Emerging Contaminants? column, which would be caught by the grepl('Yes', emerging_contaminants) check. But if a project description contained 'Mn' as a substring of another word (e.g., a proper noun or abbreviation), it could produce false positives due to the short pattern length.
suggestion: Consider using word-boundary anchors around 'Mn' in ec_str (e.g., '\bMn\b') to reduce false positives.

issue: The script has a specific fix: project_id 'DW23261801' -> 'DW232618 01', suggesting the source CSV has this value without the space. The Q1 files show project IDs with a space before the suffix (e.g., 'DW220482 03'). If fread reads the numeric-looking suffix as part of a number and drops formatting, or if the CSV literally has 'DW23261801', str_squish would not insert the missing space. The fix handles this one known case, but other similarly malformed IDs may exist.
suggestion: Audit all project_id values post-cleaning for the expected pattern 'DW[digits] [2-digit suffix]' to catch any other missing-space cases.

issue: The script passes disadvantaged_community directly to disadvantaged without normalization (no str_squish or case_when). In Q4 files the column is 'Disadvantaged\nCommunity?' which after clean_names becomes 'disadvantaged_community'. Values appear to be 'Yes' and 'No' only, but any trailing whitespace or capitalization variant would pass through uncleaned.
suggestion: Apply str_squish() to disadvantaged_community before assigning to disadvantaged, and consider a case_when to standardize to 'Yes'/'No'/'No Information'.
